title: The Presale Showroom Is Not Your Unit: Ask to See Your Real Unit
seoTitle: The Presale Showroom Is Not Your Unit: Ask This Question
description: The presale showroom shows the best unit in the building, not yours. Learn the one question to ask before you buy off-plan: show me my unit.
answer: A presale showroom is built to show the best version of the project: the best unit, the best light, the best furniture and the best view. The unit you buy will usually have a different view, a different layout and maybe a different floor. Before you sign, ask one question: show me my unit.

body:
You walk into a beautiful presale showroom and you fall in love with it. Here is the problem: you will never live in it. The showroom is not your unit. It is a stage, and it was built to sell a feeling.

## What the showroom is designed to do

A presale showroom shows the project at its very best. It is the best unit, with the best light, the best furniture and the best view. Every detail is chosen to make you imagine your life there.

There is nothing wrong with that. Developers need to sell before they build, and the showroom helps buyers picture something that does not exist yet. But it is marketing. It sells the dream of the building, not the specific home you are about to pay for.

## How your unit is different

The unit you actually buy is usually not the one you walked through. In my experience, three things change:

- **The view.** Your windows may face another street, another building or another direction.
- **The layout.** Your floor plan may be smaller, shaped differently or arranged in another way.
- **The floor.** You may be many floors lower than the space you saw, with different light and a different outlook.

Each one of these changes how the home feels and what it is worth to you. Together, they can make your unit a very different product from the one in the showroom.

## The one question to ask

Before you sign, ask one simple question: "Show me my unit."

Not the model. Not the penthouse. Your unit. Ask to see:

1. The exact floor plan of the unit you are buying, with its real dimensions.
2. The direction it faces and what the view will be from that floor.
3. Where it sits in the building, including the floor and its position on that floor.

A developer who knows their project should be able to answer this clearly. If the answer is vague, you have learned something important before you committed your deposit.

## Buy the unit, not the dream

The showroom sold the dream. Your unit is what you are buying. Keep those two things separate in your head and you will make a better decision. Enjoy the showroom, but judge the purchase on the home you will actually own.
takeaways: The presale showroom shows the best unit in the building, not the one you will buy.
Your unit can have a different view, a different layout and a different floor.
Before you sign, ask the developer to show you your exact unit.
A vague answer about your unit is a warning sign worth taking seriously.
The showroom sells the dream; your unit is the actual purchase.
faq: Is the presale model unit the same as the unit I buy?
Usually not. The model or showroom unit is often the best unit in the project, and your unit may have a different view, layout and floor.
What should I ask before buying a presale condo?
Ask the developer to show you your exact unit: the real floor plan, the direction it faces, the view from that floor and its position in the building.
Why do presale showrooms look so good?
They are designed to sell a feeling. They use the best light, furniture and views so buyers can imagine a building that does not exist yet.
